## Today

- Why majority rule still needs limits
- Enumerated and prohibited powers
- Bicameralism, judicial review, and other brakes
- Bill of Rights — especially 9 and 10

A congressional majority can still become tyranny of the majority. Aristotle and Madison both warn that popular forms can serve the many for themselves.

Congress has the powers the Constitution grants — not whatever a majority wants. Some powers are prohibited outright. Bicameralism, presentment, judicial review, federalism, and the Ninth and Tenth Amendments are the brakes.
